name: United States
summary: A broad, structured system with many programs and a clear match process for international graduates.
languageRequirement: English proficiency; OET or TOEFL commonly used for ECFMG pathways
citizenshipTimeline: Commonly 5 years as a lawful permanent resident before naturalisation eligibility; 3 years for qualifying spouses of US citizens.
requirements: Clinical experience and letters of recommendation
steps: Create an ECFMG account and verify your medical school
Complete USMLE exams and ECFMG certification
Build US clinical experience and apply through ERAS
Interview and participate in the NRMP Match

name: United Kingdom
summary: A nationally coordinated pathway with defined portfolio stages and a strong emphasis on evidence of capability.
languageRequirement: IELTS Academic or OET Medicine, unless an exemption applies
citizenshipTimeline: Usually 5 years of residence plus settled status or ILR for 12 months; some spouse routes differ.
requirements: PLAB or accepted alternative registration route
GMC registration and right to work
steps: Pass PLAB 1 and PLAB 2 where required
Apply for GMC registration with a licence to practise
Build NHS experience and apply through Oriel

name: Australia
summary: A supportive but competitive route with general registration stages and a practical focus on supervised work.
languageRequirement: IELTS, OET, PTE Academic, or TOEFL iBT
citizenshipTimeline: Generally 4 years lawful residence including the last 12 months as a permanent resident, subject to absence rules.
requirements: AMC portfolio and primary source verification
AMC CAT MCQ and clinical assessment or approved pathway
steps: Progress through general or specialist training

name: Canada
summary: A high-barrier pathway with excellent training quality and province-specific application requirements.
licensingBody: Medical Council of Canada and provincial colleges
languageRequirement: English or French proficiency, depending on province
citizenshipTimeline: Generally 1,095 days physically present in the last 5 years, with other conditions.
requirements: Medical Council of Canada account and source verification
Proof of citizenship or immigration status for many programs
steps: Complete MCC exams and language requirements

name: Germany
summary: A state-administered route where strong German language skills are central to clinical practice and licensing.
languageRequirement: German B2 plus medical language exam, usually C1 Medizin
citizenshipTimeline: Generally 5 years of lawful habitual residence, with language, livelihood, and other legal requirements.
steps: Reach the required German language level
Submit documents to the relevant state authority
Pass the Fachsprachprüfung and any knowledge exam
Obtain Approbation and apply to hospitals

name: Ireland
summary: An English-speaking European route with a mix of national registration and hospital-led training opportunities.
citizenshipTimeline: Generally 5 years reckonable residence in the last 9 years, including 1 continuous year immediately before applying.
steps: Apply for an intern or specialist training route

name: Saudi Arabia
summary: A rapidly developing health system with training opportunities coordinated through national accreditation.
languageRequirement: English used widely in training; Arabic helps with patient communication
citizenshipTimeline: Naturalisation is discretionary and not a standard fixed student-to-passport route; long residence alone does not guarantee citizenship.
requirements: Prometric or approved assessment where applicable

name: United Arab Emirates
summary: A multi-emirate system with respected clinical centres and licensing rules that vary by authority.
licensingBody: DHA, DOH, or MOHAP depending on emirate
languageRequirement: English widely used; authority-specific evidence may apply
citizenshipTimeline: Citizenship is exceptional and nomination-based for eligible categories; there is no standard student-to-passport timeline.
steps: Select the emirate and licensing authority
Apply directly through the program portal

name: Qatar
summary: A focused system centred on a small number of highly regarded institutions and structured postgraduate programs.
languageRequirement: English is the principal language of postgraduate medical education
citizenshipTimeline: Naturalisation is highly restricted and discretionary; ordinary long residence does not create an automatic passport route.
requirements: DHP eligibility and primary source verification
steps: Apply during the annual recruitment cycle
